text:
liam: Heads-up — ran a batch of concurrent prefix-cache priming experiments using the new prefetch/batching heuristics. collecting notes here.
maya: nice, did you use the replay harness or synthetic traffic?
liam: replay harness. same trace as last month but deterministic RNG and seeded kernel chooser so we can do side-by-side.
liam: command I ran:
```
./run_benchmark --trace traces/2025-user-sessions.tar.gz --mode=replay --seed=20250312 --kernel-policy=auto-select --batching=workload-adaptive --kv-prefetch=on --concurrency=64 --duration=600 --emit=metrics,logs
```
sam: quick q — how did you isolate eviction behavior vs just coldstart effects?
liam: we did a 3-phase run per seed:
  1) priming-only (no evictions allowed) to get an upper bound hit curve
  2) steady-state with eviction turned on (LRU-ish with async-sweep)
  3) hammer-phase — short burst 2x QPS to force churn
sophia: what metrics are we tracking? hit-rate by prefix length? tail p99/p999?
liam: tracked: overall KV hit-rate, hit-rate by prefix-length buckets (1-16,17-64,65+), per-token latency (p50,p95,p99,p999), kernel-switch count, and retry/incorrect-eviction counters from the runtime.
jun: curious about "incorrect-eviction" — did you hit the bug we saw last sprint?
liam: yeah, saw a reproducible spike in incorrect-eviction when concurrency >=48 and prefetch stride > 4. symptoms: two workers removing the same cache entry concurrently, leading to negative refcounts in the debug logs.
liam: stack snippet from runtime logs:
```
[E 2025-03-12T14:21:12Z] kv_cache.cc:423 evict_entry: refcount=-1 key=prefix_0x4f3b
[E 2025-03-12T14:21:12Z] allocator.cc:88 free_block: double-free detected
```
maya: ouch. was the allocator the root cause or the refcount race?
liam: root cause = non-atomic decrement in the fast-path. allocator alerted due to double free. fix is simple: use atomic fetch_sub with check or CAS; but need to ensure perf cost is acceptable.
sam: did you try kernel selection impacts? maybe different kernels change timing and reduce race window.
liam: yes — interestingly, kernel-policy=auto-select picked MiniKernelA under short sequences and MiniKernelB under long ones. MiniKernelB has a tighter prefetch schedule which increased parallelism and exposed the race more often.
sophia: any numbers we can share? even rough.
liam: summary from a 600s run (seed=20250312, concurrency=64):
  - priming-only hit-rate: 78.1%
  - steady-state with eviction: 62.4% (p50 token latency +9ms vs priming)
  - hammer-phase hit-rate: 54.2%
  - incorrect-eviction events: 0 in priming-only, 17 in steady-state, 92 during hammer-phase
  - p99 token latency increased from 34ms -> 89ms during hammer
  - kernel-switch count per request doubled in hammer-phase
jun: That many incorrect-evictions is rough. Do we have a repro script/trace to hand off to infra?
liam: pushed the trace + run config to s3: s3://redwood-perf/bugs/2025-03-12-prefetch-race.tar.gz
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Reminder: nightly stability cluster uses kernel-policy=conservative which should avoid MiniKernelB. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/repo/runbooks/kv-eviction
maya: next steps suggested:
  - short-term: patch to atomic refcount + smoke tests (low risk)
  - mid-term: add deterministic kernel-seeding to replay harness to ensure apples-to-apples kernel mix when comparing PRs
  - long-term: add a microbench that stresses eviction under kernel-induced timing to quantify perf cost of atomic ops
sam: for the smoke tests, can we gate with a perf budget? i.e. make change require <2% p50 regression on the microbench.
sophia: agree. also add a correctness E2E that asserts no negative refcounts and no double frees for 10k concurrent ephemeral keys.
liam: I've already got a branch with atomic change: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3142 — runs show ~0.7% p50 regression locally but correctness fixed.
jun: let's run a CI matrix: (seeded replay x 3 seeds) x (kernel-policy=auto,conservative) x (concurrency 16,48,64) and compare.
liam: will kick that off tomorrow and post results. also will add a small script to normalize kernel counts between runs so we get fair comparisons.
qa-runner: I'll add the trace to the QA harness and schedule a 3-run smoke matrix overnight. will report failures to this thread.
maya: thanks — please include raw metric exports (prometheus snapshots) and runtime logs. for PR review include the microbench results and the seeded replay comparators.
liam: ack. TL;DR: found concurrency-induced incorrect-eviction, likely widened by kernel timing; quick fix = atomic refcount (small perf hit), follow-ups = deterministic kernel mix for replay and targeted microbench. assigning follow-ups in the PR.
sam: :thumbsup: keep the thread updated.
ops-bot: [ci] Job scheduled: perf-matrix-2025-03-13 (links: https://ci.internal/jobs/98765)
liam: dropping artifacts here when available.
